In modern usage, Jean is a versatile name, suitable for both males and females, symbolizing spiritual growth and devotion.

historical_references.reference: Jeanne d'Arc, also known as Joan of Arc, was a heroic French peasant girl who emerged as the 'Maid of Orléans' during the Hundred Years' War (1337-1453) between England and France. She claimed to have divine messages from saints, dressing in masculine attire and leading the French army to several important victories, including the relief of Orléans in 1429.

Saint Jeanne de Chateau-Thierry, also known as Joan of Arc of the Blessed Sacrament, was a French Catholic saint who lived in the 17th century. Born in Dijon, she experienced visions and ecstasies from a very young age, and was known for her devotion to the Blessed Sacrament. She spent most of her life as a hermit in a small cell in the chapel of a monastery in Chateau-Thierry, where she received countless visitors.
